ety.text: Borrowed from Latin focus (“hearth, fireplace”); see there for more. Related to fuel. Kepler introduced the term into mathematics and the sciences in describing elliptical orbits of planets (quote from Nicholas Mee): "One of the interesting properties of an ellipse is that if there were a light bulb at one focus, then all the light that it emits would reflect off the ellipse and converge at the other focus. This is why Kepler originally used the name focus for these points."

senses.d: A point at which reflected or refracted rays of light converge.
ex: The heat of sunlight at the focus of a magnifying glass can easily set dry leaves on fire.

senses.d: A point of a conic at which rays reflected from a curve or surface converge.
The fact of the convergence of light on the photographic medium.
ex: Unfortunately, the license plate is out of focus in this image.

senses.d: The quality of the convergence of light on the photographic medium.
ex: During this scene, the boy’s face shifts subtly from soft focus into sharp focus.

senses.d: Concentration of attention.
ex: I believe I can bring the high degree of focus required for this important job.

senses.d: Something to which activity, attention or interest is primarily directed.
ex: My studies are my main focus right now.

senses.d: The exact point of where an earthquake occurs, in three dimensions (underneath the epicentre).
ex: The earthquake's focus was at exactly 37 degrees north, 18 degrees south, seventy five meters below the ground.

senses.d: The status of being the currently active element in a user interface, often indicated by a visual highlight.
ex: Text entered at the keyboard or pasted from a clipboard is sent to the component which currently has the focus.

senses.d: The most important word or phrase in a sentence or passage, or the one that imparts information.
An object used in casting a magic spell.
To cause (rays of light, etc) to converge at a single point.
To adjust (a lens, an optical instrument) in order to position an image with respect to the focal plane.
ex: You'll need to focus the microscope carefully in order to capture the full detail of this surface.

senses.d: To adjust itself or be adjusted such that light from a scene converges appropriately to create a clear image.
ex: I can't get the lens to focus.
The camera focuses automatically on the subject's eyes.

senses.d: To direct attention, effort, or energy to a particular audience or task.
ex: The president focused her remarks on the newcomers.

senses.d: To concentrate one’s attention.
ex: If you're going to beat your competitors, you need to focus.

senses.d: To concentrate one's attention on something; to have as one's central point of interest, concern, etc.
ex: I have to focus on my work.

senses.d: To transfer the input focus to (a visual element), so that it receives subsequent input.
ex: The text box won't receive the user's keystrokes unless you explicitly focus it.

senses.d: To aggregate figures of accounts.

senses.d: Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus (definite location).
ex: focal point
The contamination was focal.

senses.d: Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus of attention.
ex: focal point
The disturbances at the periphery became a focal concern later in the investigation.

senses.d: Limited to a small area.
ex: The rash was focal.

senses.d: One of two lines perpendicular to the axis of a cone such that the cosine of the angle between the line and the axis is equal to the ratio of the cosines o the semiangles of the cone.
An object that is used to focus concentration when performing magic.
ex: Choose your focals to blend well with the intention of your magical work or ritual.
And no witch leaves behind focals.

senses.d: The individual who is the focus of a study or review, when the study or review is based on that individual's interactions with others.
ex: Relevancy provides focals motivation to change by making the links clear between their behavior and the success of the organization.

senses.d: A representative of a group or class of people within an organizational system.
ex: Consolidate all focals' requirements: To be done by the Operations Manager.

senses.d: A sign or similar type of marketing material designed to draw attention to special deals.
The central or most important element of something; a focal element.
ex: When using supporting flowers, consider their size and shape in relation to the focals and how the colour supports and enhances them.

senses.d: A major point of interest; an attraction.
An exemplar of a concept.
